assertions.description: window.launchQueue is exposed — the queue through which focus-existing launches are delivered into an existing document.
LaunchQueue.prototype.setConsumer is a function — the consumer is where the granted activation is observed.
LaunchParams exposes targetURL and files, which the consumer uses to decide what to do with the activation (route a URL, open a launched file).
assertions.test: typeof LaunchParams === 'function' && 'targetURL' in LaunchParams.prototype && 'files' in LaunchParams.prototype

assertions.description: navigator.userActivation exposes boolean isActive and hasBeenActive — the documented feature-detection surface (read isActive inside the launchQueue consumer).
assertions.test: (()=>{const u=navigator.userActivation;return !!u && typeof u.isActive==='boolean' && typeof u.hasBeenActive==='boolean' && 'isActive' in UserActivation.prototype;})()

assertions.description: For a user-initiated launch that launch_handler "focus-existing" delivers into an already-open, in-scope document, navigator.userActivation.isActive is true inside the launchQueue consumer and window.open() returns a window (Chromium browser_test WebAppLaunchHandlerBrowserTest.FocusExistingGrantsUserActivation).
assertions.test: Requires an installed web app with launch_handler focus-existing and a second user-initiated launch (shortcut, OS launcher, captured link or file) into its open window; installation cannot be automated from a page. Verify with the consumer-activation-probe concept.

assertions.description: No activation is granted by this step for navigating launches (navigate-new, navigate-existing, or the launch that creates the window), for launches not initiated by the user, or when LaunchParams are re-delivered for the same launch (e.g. after a reload): exactly one activation per user launch.
assertions.test: Requires an installed app and OS-level launches; the initial-launch half is pinned by the browser_test expecting isActive false after the first launch. Verify with the when-activation-is-withheld concept.
